original_question: For a locally compact group G, how can one characterize when the Fourier algebra A(G) is pseudo-amenable and when it is approximately amenable?
target_in_paper: The open question in the paper’s Fourier-algebra discussion asking whether, for a locally compact group G, approximate amenability of A(G) is equivalent to pseudo-amenability, hence equivalent to the existence of an approximate identity in A(G).
correct_elements: The draft correctly identifies the ambient object—a locally compact group G and its Fourier algebra A(G)—and it focuses on exactly the two generalized amenability notions discussed there: pseudo-amenability and approximate amenability.
missing_details: The paper does not pose a broad two-part characterization problem from scratch; rather, it records that the pseudo-amenable case is already settled and isolates the remaining sharp question about approximate amenability.
The pseudo-amenability side is already characterized in the nearby discussion: A(G) is pseudo-amenable if and only if A(G) has an approximate identity.
The relevant approximate identity is not assumed bounded; that distinction is part of the point.
The paper’s unresolved issue is whether approximate amenability coincides with that already-known pseudo-amenability criterion.
The nearby context also records the sufficient condition that A(G) is approximately amenable when G is amenable; the draft does not mention this known half of the story.
The algebra under discussion is the complex Fourier algebra A(G) in the Banach-algebra sense, not the operator-space variants such as operator approximate amenability or operator pseudo-amenability.
The question should be quantified explicitly as applying to every locally compact group G.
refined_question: For every locally compact group G, with A(G) its complex Fourier algebra, is A(G) approximately amenable if and only if it is pseudo-amenable; equivalently, is A(G) approximately amenable exactly when A(G) has an approximate identity (not necessarily bounded)?
equivalent_formulation: For every locally compact group G, does the existence of an approximate identity in A(G) characterize approximate amenability of A(G)?
justification: Your draft points to the Fourier-algebra discussion, but it is broader than the paper’s actual target. In that discussion, the pseudo-amenable side is already given a precise criterion—pseudo-amenability is equivalent to the existence of an approximate identity—while the genuinely sharp remaining issue is whether approximate amenability is the same thing for A(G). The surrounding context also notes the known sufficient result that A(G) is approximately amenable whenever G is amenable. So the paper-faithful stand-alone question is not an open-ended request to characterize both notions independently, but the narrower question of whether approximate amenability coincides with the already-settled pseudo-amenability/approximate-identity condition.
